notice: EXAMPLE CONFIGURATION - NOT A REVIEWED SETTLEMENT SPEC. verification.status is UNVERIFIED and no reviewer is named, so this spec blocks model-dependent strategy activation (handoff section 9.2, WP-110 acceptance 3). VENUE-SETL-1 redrafted the values below on 2026-10-04, and revised them after its first review round the same day, from public evidence recorded in docs/settlement/btc-15m-updown-review.md and docs/venue/verified-2026-10-04.md: the market rules text (sha256 485ceb1dabc4aa12fb42c76184563b7378f01e5de9ded73df049c0d191cd5ad1, byte-identical on all 31 btc-up-or-down-15m windows read that open at or after 2026-08-07T00:00Z, and on 100 more resolved windows read later that day), the official Polymarket changelog entries of 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-14, the Polymarket PolyBolt TWAP channel reference, and the Chainlink Data Streams TWAP documentation and stream directory. Where a value below rests on observation or inference rather than documentation, it says so. No human has reviewed them. Before this spec may be marked reviewed, a person must answer every line of docs/settlement/btc-15m-updown-review-checklist.md, the report-selection question (venue report U-24) must be answered and written into a redraft, a rules version must exist to name (no catalog rules-version row exists for these markets yet), and the window must be confirmed against the windows the feed publishes at that time.

settlementSpec.resolutionSource: Chainlink Data Streams BTC/USD 60-second TWAP stream: the market rules text names the BTC/USD TWAP data stream at https://data.chain.link/streams/btc-usd-twap-60s-streams. Chainlink's public stream directory lists a live stream named BTC/USD-Streams-TWAP-60s-mainnet-production (report schema v2); that it is the stream the rules' URL names is an inference, because the rules' page could not be read (venue report F-32, U-31). Chainlink also lists a separate live BTC/USD 30-second TWAP stream, which the rules do not name. Polymarket documents its 60-second Chainlink TWAP series as the prices used by crypto up/down market resolution (PolyBolt channel price.crypto.twap, which requires CLOB API credentials).
settlementSpec.windowStartRule: Sixty seconds (windowSeconds) before the end of the settlement value's averaging window, which windowEndRule defines; it is therefore not necessarily 60 seconds before the market close. The 60-second length is documented: Polymarket's 2026-08-07 changelog gives 15-minute markets a 60-second lookback, and Chainlink's example is a 60-second TWAP, requested at 12:05:01, that covers the interval from 12:04:01 through 12:05:01. Neither Polymarket nor Chainlink documents whether the start boundary is inclusive.
settlementSpec.windowEndRule: The settlement value is the price of one report of the BTC/USD 60-second TWAP stream, the report selected for the market close (the end of the title's range; see timestampBoundary). This is the review's reading R2, an inference rather than a documented rule: Polymarket documents that the final settlement price comes from the applicable TWAP feed with a 60-second lookback, but not the instant at which it is read (venue report C-15). Its 60-second averaging window is anchored to that report's latest observation, not to the market close: Chainlink documents that a TWAP window is anchored to the latest observation and does not align to the clock, its example window ends at the moment requested, and it defines observationsTimestamp as when a report's price was last observed. On that reading, the window ends at the market close only when the selected report's observationsTimestamp equals the close. Which report Polymarket selects for the close is undocumented (venue report U-24): candidates include the report observed exactly at the close, the report whose validFromTimestamp-to-observationsTimestamp window contains the close (Chainlink's rule for the price at a given moment, under which that price can be observed after the moment), and the first report after it. This spec names no selection. A settlement value that cannot be tied to one identified report and its timestamps is ambiguous, and entries halt (fallbackSource).
settlementSpec.referenceOpenSource: The same BTC/USD 60-second TWAP stream's value for the market open (the start of the title's range, the rules' 'price at the beginning of that range'; see timestampBoundary), which Polymarket calls the price to beat; its 2026-08-07 changelog states that both the price to beat and the final settlement price come from the applicable TWAP feed. As at the close, the value is the price of one stream report, whose 60-second averaging window is anchored to that report's latest observation and therefore need not end at the open instant. Which report Polymarket selects for the open is undocumented (venue report U-24), and this spec names none; an opening value that cannot be tied to one identified report is ambiguous, and entries halt. It is not a spot price.
settlementSpec.timestampBoundary: The market window is the time range in the market title, which the rules name ('the time range specified in the title'); the title says ET, so the range is read in America/New_York time. The window opens at the range's start and closes at its end, 900 seconds later. Instants are compared in UTC, converted under America/New_York rules (for example, UTC-4 until 2026-11-01T06:00Z and UTC-5 from then). A title whose range does not convert to exactly one 900-second UTC interval is ambiguous, and entries halt for that window: computed, not yet observed, on 2026-11-01 the repeated 01:00-02:00 ET hour gives the windows opening at 05:00Z and 06:00Z, 05:15Z and 06:15Z, and 05:30Z and 06:30Z the same ET range (venue report U-34). Observed, not documented (venue report F-15, U-29): on all 115 windows read on 2026-10-04, Gamma eventStartTime and endDate matched the title range's start and end, and the epoch in the slug matched its start; they can locate a window but do not define it. On the same windows Gamma startDate was about 24 hours before the open; it is not the window open, and its meaning is undocumented. Whether the open and close instants are inclusive is undocumented (venue report U-24).
settlementSpec.roundingRule: No rounding: the settlement value and the opening value are compared as exact decimals at the precision the stream publishes. Polymarket does not document the precision of its comparison (venue report U-25), and rounding can change the outcome of a near-tie. The eventMetadata priceToBeat and finalPrice numbers Polymarket publishes are binary floating-point values and are never used for settlement here.
settlementSpec.fallbackSource: None. If the stream value for either boundary is unavailable or ambiguous, including a value whose stream report cannot be identified, halt entries for the series and escalate to the operator; no substitute source is used and no value is interpolated. Polymarket documents no fallback source for this series.
settlementSpec.disputePolicy: Halt entries for the market, keep the position observable, and settle nothing while a dispute is open; a dispute is an in-flight process, not an outcome. Windows of this series were observed to resolve automatically 53 to 152 seconds after the close (100 resolved windows opening 2026-10-03T22:45Z to 2026-10-04T23:30Z, read on 2026-10-04; median 55 seconds); whether, and for how long, such a resolution can be disputed is not documented.
settlementSpec.clarificationPolicy: On any post-open clarification, whether an Additional context update or any change to the rules text or its sha256, halt entries for the series and require a fresh human review of this spec against the amended rules before the series resumes.
